questions.question: Which statement describes a public cloud?

options.text: Infrastructure used exclusively by one organisation in its own datacenter
Infrastructure owned by a provider and offered to multiple customers over the internet
options.why: Correct. That is the public cloud model.

options.text: A combination of on-premises and cloud resources
A cloud where all customer data is publicly readable
options.why: "Public" refers to availability to customers, not data visibility.

questions.explanation: Public cloud infrastructure is owned by a provider such as Microsoft and shared by many isolated customers.

questions.question: Which TWO are characteristics of the public cloud?

options.text: No capital expenditure is required to start
options.why: Correct. You do not buy hardware.

options.text: The customer maintains the physical servers
Resources can be provisioned quickly on demand
The customer must build its own datacenter
options.why: Not required in the public cloud.

questions.explanation: Public cloud removes up-front hardware costs and lets you provision resources on demand.

questions.scenario: A start-up wants to launch a web app quickly with no hardware purchase and expects unpredictable traffic.
questions.question: Which cloud model is the most appropriate?

options.why: Private cloud needs dedicated infrastructure and investment.
Correct. No CapEx, quick start and elastic capacity.
This requires buying hardware and has fixed capacity.

options.text: None. Web apps cannot run in the cloud
options.why: Web apps are one of the most common cloud workloads.

questions.explanation: The public cloud is the natural fit for fast starts and unpredictable demand.

questions.question: In a public cloud, many customers share the same physical hardware while being isolated from each other. What is this called?

options.why: Correct. Multiple tenants share infrastructure with logical isolation.
Vertical scaling means making a single resource bigger.
Geo-redundancy is about copying data to another region.

questions.explanation: Multi-tenancy is the sharing of infrastructure between isolated customers, the foundation of public cloud economics.
